units.title: Basic concepts of cellular energetics and metabolism
units.summary: Basic Concepts of Cellular Energetics and Metabolism • Cellular Energetics • Processes that a cell obtains, transforms, applies energy. • These may include: • Exergonic chemical reactions that release energy • And endergonic chemical reactions that consume energy • All these reactions are collectively known as metabolism • Metabolism • Sum total of all biochemical reactions occuring in cell Basic Concepts of Cellular Energetics and Metabolism • Metabolic reactions are divided into • Anabolism • Reactions that use smaller molecules to build larger molecule. using amino acids to make protein • Cellular energy is used in these processes. • Catabolism • Reactions that break down complex molecules to simple molecules • Cellular energy is produced in these processes.

units.title: Nature and functions of enzymes
units.summary: Nature and Functions of Enzymes • Most cellular reactions are organic reactions that occur slowly without catalysts. Therefore, there are many enzymes in human body to control rates of different reactions. • Enzyme • Chemical nature: Specific sub-class of protein • Active site: Special 3-dimension conformation for binding of specific molecule • Function: Catalyze chemical reactions of specific molecule • Charactersitic: Do not change after the reaction Nature and Functions of Enzymes Three steps are involved in enzyme action Nature and Functions of Enzymes • The function of each enzyme is specific • Acting on specific substrate that fits with shape of active site • Names of enzymes usually end in “ase” and are often named for the reaction they catalyze • Example • ATPase catalyzes • ATP ↔ ADP + Phosphate • Lipase catalyzes • Triglyceride ↔ Monoglyceride + Fatty acids

units.title: Concepts of homeostasis
units.summary: Concepts of Homeostasis • The rate of chemical reactions in human body must be controlled to keep healthy body conditions. Therefore, human body must be able to maintain stable and balance internal environment by various methods. These ways are collectively known as “homeostasis”. • Common ways to maintain homeostasis • (1) Negative feedback mechanisms • (2) Positive feedback mechanisms Concepts of Homeostasis • (1) Negative feedback mechanism • Most homeostatic control methods are negative feedback mechanisms.

units.title: Examples of homeostasis
units.summary: Examples of Homeostasis Negative feedback mechanism: Stimulus: Bleeding Responses: Stop bleeding This is an example demonstrating “positive feedback cycle as a part of negative feedback control system”. Examples of Homeostasis Homeostatic range Remark Variable Body Temperature 35.8-38.2ºC Blood pH 7.35-7.45 Blood Pressure 60-90 mmHg/ 90-140 mmHg Heart Rate 60-100 bpm Fasting Blood Glucose 3.9-5.6 mmol/L WHO (2025)
